page: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in CPU-intensive tasks, with the PassMark CPU score, extended instructions test, and encryption test all placing in the top 10%. Multi-core capabilities are strong, as evidenced by top 25% placements in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 6623.14 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50%.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, and static web serving, where it demonstrates strong benchmark throughput. It also supports moderate LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing on small to medium models. However, text generation on large 70B models is a notable tradeoff, registering in the bottom 25% at 2.75 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for high-density, multi-threaded enterprise applications that require significant memory and network throughput without the added cost of specialized GPU hardware.
